exam: JPSC Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination 2025 (Advt. No. 01/2026)
paper: General Studies Paper-I - Question Booklet Series A (held 19.04.2026)

questions.q: The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) was composed by
questions.e: Harishena, court poet of Samudragupta, composed the Prayaga Prashasti in Sanskrit.

questions.q:
Statement (I): The Amaranayaka system was a major political innovation of the Vijayanagara empire.
Statement (II): The Amaranayakas were military commanders who were given territories to govern, from which they collected taxes to maintain a stipulated contingent of horses and elephants for Raja (King).
o: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct and Statement (II) is the correct explanation for Statement (I).
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct and Statement (II) is not the correct explanation for Statement (I).
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
questions.e: Amaranayakas were Vijayanagara military chiefs given territories (amaram) to collect revenue and maintain troops, which explains the system's innovation.

questions.q:
Statement (I): In the Mughal Agrarian system, the Zamindars were considered the owners of all the lands in their domain.
Statement (II): The Zamindars were a class of landed intermediaries who enjoyed certain hereditary rights in land and collected revenue on behalf of the state, but the actual cultivation was done by peasants (Ryots).
o: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct and Statement (II) is the correct explanation for Statement (I).
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct and Statement (II) is not the correct explanation for Statement (I).
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
questions.e: Mughal zamindars were hereditary revenue intermediaries, not owners of all land; so Statement I is wrong and II is right.

questions.q: The ‘Radcliffe line’ demarcated the boundary between
questions.e: The Radcliffe Line (1947) drew the India-Pakistan boundary in Punjab and Bengal.

questions.q: Who was the last Mughal emperor at the time of the Revolt of 1857?
questions.e: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the Mughal emperor in 1857 and was exiled to Rangoon.

questions.q: Who was the chairman of the drafting Committee of the constituent Assembly?
questions.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.q:
With reference to the Permanent Settlement Act (1793), consider the following statements:
I) The land revenue to be paid to the company was fixed permanently
II) Zamindars were recognised as the owners of land, subject to payment of revenue
III) The settlement ensured security of tenure and protection from eviction to peasants
IV) The system was introduced during the Governor-Generalship of Lord Cornwallis
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Cornwallis's Permanent Settlement fixed revenue permanently and made zamindars owners; it gave no tenure security to peasants.

questions.q:
Match the following Acts with their associated features or consequences:
A) Rowlatt Act (1919)  1) Provincial Autonomy
B) Government of India Act, 1919  2) Detention without trial
C) Vernacular Press Act (1878)  3) Introduction of Dyarchy in provinces
D) Government of India Act, 1935  4) Curb on Indian Language Newspapers
questions.e: Rowlatt Act - detention without trial; GoI Act 1919 - dyarchy; Vernacular Press Act - curbs on Indian-language papers; GoI Act 1935 - provincial autonomy.

questions.q: With reference to the agrarian society in Mughal india, the term 'Khud-Khasht' and ‘Pahi-Kasht' refers to
o: Two types of land revenue systems
Two types of Peasants (Residents Vs Non-residents/migrants)
questions.e: Khud-kasht were resident cultivators and pahi-kasht were non-resident/migrant peasants.

questions.q:
Match the Medieval terms with their meanings:
A) Khutba  1) A sermon read in the name of the ruler during Friday prayers
B) Sijda  2) Land Revenue assignment in the Delhi Sultanate
C) Iqta  3) Prostration before the monarch (introduced by Balban)
D) Tankas  4) Silver coins introduced by Iltutmish
questions.e: Khutba - Friday sermon in the ruler's name; Sijda - prostration (Balban); Iqta - revenue assignment; Tanka - silver coin of Iltutmish.

questions.q: With references to the religious history of medieval India, the Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis were associated with:
o: Advocating renunciation and meditation to realise the Formless reality (Nirguna Bhakti)
questions.e: Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis advocated renunciation and meditation on the formless (nirguna) reality.

questions.q:
Match the Harappan sites with their specific features:
A) Chanhudaro  1) Evidence of ploughed field
B) Kalibangan  2) Specialized center for craft production (bead making)
C) Dholavira  3) Terracotta models of the plough
D) Banawali  4) Large water reservoirs
questions.e: Chanhudaro - bead making; Kalibangan - ploughed field; Dholavira - water reservoirs; Banawali - terracotta plough.

questions.q:
Match the Ancient texts with their Subjects/Authors:
A) Ashtadhyayi  1) Earliest Sanskrit grammar by Panini
B) Charaka Samhita  2) Encyclopedia of Indian Medicine (Ayurveda)
C) Mudrarakshasa  3) Play by Vishakhadatta describing Mauryan Politics
D) Silappadikaram  4) Tamil Epic about Kovalan and Kannagi
questions.e: Ashtadhyayi (Panini grammar), Charaka Samhita (Ayurveda), Mudrarakshasa (Vishakhadatta), Silappadikaram (Kovalan-Kannagi).

questions.q: The term ‘Sarthavaha' mentioned in ancient inscriptions and texts refers to
o: The chief judicial officer of the village
The leader of the merchant caravan
The Officer in charge of royal elephants
The Priest performing the Ashvamedha sacrifice
questions.e: A Sarthavaha was the leader of a merchant caravan.

questions.q: Who among the following was the first to decipher the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts used in the inscriptions of Ashoka
questions.e: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi (1837) and Kharosthi scripts of the Ashokan edicts.

questions.q: Public Administration is the study of
o: Public Administration dynamics of the states
questions.e: Public administration is chiefly concerned with implementing public policy.

questions.q: Which of the following governance models is most aligned with the principles of participatory democracy and decentralization.
questions.e: Pluralistic governance spreads power among many groups, fitting participatory democracy and decentralisation.

questions.q: Under which case did the supreme court of India include the right to education with in the right to life?
o: Frank Anthony Public School employees federation Vs Union of India (1986)
questions.e: In Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992) the Supreme Court read the right to education into Article 21.

questions.q: Which of the following statement are correct?
o: Local government derived authority from the state government and are subordinates to it
Local government are dependent on the state government
Local Government derived their authority from the constitution
Local government perform function in the interest of the nation
questions.e: After the 73rd and 74th Amendments, local governments draw constitutional authority (Parts IX and IX-A).

questions.q:
Match List I (Features) with List II (Related to) and select the correct answer:
i) Democratic decentralisation  a) 73rd Amendment
ii) Nagar panchayats  b) 74th Amendment
iii) Panchayati Raj elections  c) B.R. Mehta Committee
iv) Two Tier system  d) Ashok Mehta Committee
questions.e: Democratic decentralisation - Balwant Rai Mehta; Nagar panchayats - 74th Amendment; PRI elections - 73rd Amendment; two-tier system - Ashok Mehta.

questions.q:
Which part of the Indian constitution declares India to be a welfare state?
I) Part III
II) Part IV
III) Part IX
IV) Part VI
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.e: The Directive Principles in Part IV aim at a welfare state.

questions.q:
Can the Indian federal system become unitary?
I) During the external emergency
II) If supported by the majority in the Lok Sabha
III) On proposal supported by a two-third majority in both houses of the parliament
IV) During the presidential election
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.e: During a national emergency on grounds of external aggression the federal system works in a unitary manner.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I) The Aravalli ranges prevent the eastward expansion of the desert
II) The Aravalli range is a major watershed/water divide
III) The Aravalli mountains have the greatest impact on the climate of Rajasthan
IV) The Aravalli ranges extend from Delhi to Ahmedabad
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.e: All four statements on the Aravallis (desert barrier, water divide, climatic influence, Delhi-Gujarat extent) are accepted.

questions.q: Which of the following is not correctly match?
questions.e: The Nilgiris are a block (horst) mountain, not volcanic.

questions.q: Which of the following states is also known as the “Land of Red river and Blue hills"?
questions.e: Assam, with the Brahmaputra and surrounding hills, is called the land of red river and blue hills.

questions.q: The total length of India's coastline, including islands, is kilometres.
questions.e: India's revised coastline length (including islands) is 11,098.81 km.

questions.q: Which of the following islands is of volcanic origin?
questions.e: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is India's only active volcano.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct order of distribution of scheduled tribes of India from South to North
questions.e: South to north: Kota (Nilgiris), Warli (Maharashtra), Bhil (western-central India), Gaddi (Himachal).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about population distribution in India:
I) Physiography strongly influences population distribution and density
II) Northern plains have high density due to fertile soils and water availability
III) Peninsular Plateau uniformity shows low density
questions.e: Physiography and fertile northern plains explain density patterns; the plateau is not uniformly low-density.

questions.q: Which one of the following industries is not a ‘Weight loss industry‘?
questions.e: Cotton textiles do not lose much weight in processing, unlike paper, cement or iron and steel.

questions.q: Jhum cultivation is an important economic activity in Northeast India. This activity falls into which group?
questions.e: Jhum (shifting cultivation) is agriculture, a primary activity.

questions.q: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
questions.e: Ashtamudi in Kerala is a backwater/lagoon lake, not a fluvial lake.

questions.q: When was the 'Doha Development Round' of WTO be begun?
questions.e: The Doha Development Round was launched at the WTO Ministerial in November 2001.

questions.q: Which one of the following states was least urbanised according to 2011 census?
questions.e: Himachal Pradesh had the lowest urban share (about 10%) in Census 2011.

questions.q: When was the National Human Right Commission established in India?
questions.e: The NHRC was set up on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act.

questions.q: Who is the Chairperson of National Disaster management Authority of India?
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairperson of the NDMA.

questions.q: Who received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in the 71st National Film Award Ceremony?
questions.e: Mohanlal received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award at the 71st National Film Awards.

questions.q: When was the first ‘Earth Summit’ organised?
questions.e: The first Earth Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.

questions.q: Which one of the following gases is minimum in the atmosphere?
questions.e: Carbon dioxide (~0.04%) is far less abundant than argon (~0.93%), oxygen or nitrogen.

questions.q: How many countries was participated in the Bretton woods conference in 1944?
questions.e: Delegates of 44 Allied nations attended Bretton Woods in July 1944.

questions.q: In which state the largest portion of the slum population of India did live according to 2011 census?
questions.e: Maharashtra had the largest slum population in Census 2011.

questions.q: The term "Demographic Dividend" refers to
questions.e: Demographic dividend is the growth potential from a large working-age population.

questions.q: "Make in India" initiative was launched in
questions.e: Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014.

questions.q: Green GDP refers to
o: GDP after accounting for environmental degradation
questions.e: Green GDP adjusts GDP for environmental degradation and resource depletion.

questions.q: The vision of Viksit Bharat is built upon the "GYAN" model to ensure inclusive development. What does the acronym GYAN represents in this context?
questions.e: GYAN stands for Garib, Yuva, Annadata and Nari - the four pillars of Viksit Bharat.

questions.q: The Indian Economy is often described as having a “Leapfrogging"” structural transition. Which of the following features best illustrates this unique characteristics?
o: A dominant shift from agriculture directly to the services sector for GDP contribution, bypassing a massive industrialization phase
Achieving 100% employment in the manufacturing sector before 2026
Complete dependence on the Public sector for all heavy industries
A decline in the importance of digital economy in rural areas
questions.e: India's leapfrogging means jumping from agriculture to services-led growth, bypassing a large manufacturing phase.

questions.q: To promote a "Circular Economy" and sustainable lifestyle choices as part of the Viksit Bharat agenda. the Prime Minister launched which global mass movement at COP 26?
questions.e: Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) was announced by the PM at COP26 in Glasgow.

questions.q: Which International Organisation replaced the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in 1995, acting as a key driver for globalization?
questions.e: The WTO replaced GATT on 1 January 1995.

questions.q: Economic planning in India was inspired by
questions.e: India's Five-Year Plans were modelled on the Soviet (USSR) planning system.

questions.q: The term “Blue Economy" refers to
o: Economy based on tourism and cultural heritage
questions.e: The blue economy is the sustainable use of ocean resources for growth.

questions.q: Which Indian scheme supports small and medium enterprises?
questions.e: PM MUDRA Yojana provides collateral-free loans to micro and small enterprises.

questions.q: How many people was escaped from the multidimensional poverty in India during 2013-14 to 2022-23, according to NITI Aayog?
questions.e: NITI Aayog estimated 24.82 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty between 2013-14 and 2022-23.

questions.q: How much expenditure in the next five years has been decided on the technologies of carbon capture, utilization and storage in the central Budget of 2026-27?
questions.e: As per the official key, ₹20,000 crore over five years was set aside for CCUS technologies.

questions.q: How many days of employment has been guaranteed for a person in a year in the new VB-G RAM G Act?
questions.e: The VB-G RAM G Act raised the employment guarantee to 125 days per household a year.

questions.q: When was the world population counted 1 Billion?
questions.e: World population reached 1 billion around 1804, in the 19th century.

questions.q: Which day is celebrated as Human Rights Day
questions.e: Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December, the date the UDHR was adopted in 1948.

questions.q: Who among the following is awarded Padma Vibhushan in 2025
questions.e: Suzuki Motor's Osamu Suzuki was conferred the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 2025.

questions.q: Which among the following movies was awarded as the best Non-feature film in the 71st National Film Awards?
questions.e: 'Flowering Man' won Best Non-Feature Film at the 71st National Film Awards.

questions.q: In India, disaster management comes under which ministry
questions.e: Disaster management is the nodal responsibility of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.q: Which Indian sectors were reported to be negatively affected the most by US tariff increases?
questions.e: Textiles, gems and jewellery were the labour-intensive export sectors hit hardest by the US tariff hike.

questions.q: In which state the Khelo India youth games, 2025 took place
questions.e: The Khelo India Youth Games 2025 were held in Bihar.

questions.q: In which country the United Nations climate Conference (COP30) took place?
questions.e: COP30 was held in Belem, Brazil in November 2025.

questions.q: In which city the wildlife Institute of India is situated
questions.e: The Wildlife Institute of India is located in Dehradun.

questions.q: Which organization controls the Gaza strip since 2007?
questions.e: Hamas has controlled the Gaza Strip since 2007.

questions.q: "CAPTAIN ARJUN" is a robot which has been launched with an aim to screen passenger while they board:
questions.e: RPF's robot 'Captain Arjun' was launched at Pune railway station to screen train passengers.

questions.q: Which of the following are not the 4 Vs of Big Data?
questions.e: The 4 Vs of big data are Volume, Velocity, Variety and Veracity, not Verification.

questions.q: “PM Surya Ghar" Mission launched in which year
questions.e: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana for rooftop solar was launched in 2024.

questions.q: Which enzyme is responsible for the digestion of proteins in the stomach?
questions.e: Pepsin digests proteins in the acidic environment of the stomach.

questions.q: In 2025, Australia's Western Sydney University (WSU) is planning to setup a campus in which Indian state?
questions.e: Western Sydney University planned its India campus in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: Which of the following international agreements first imposed legally binding emission reduction targets on developed countries?
questions.e: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) first set legally binding emission targets for developed countries.

questions.q: AI first came to be known in which year?
questions.e: The term 'Artificial Intelligence' was coined at the Dartmouth conference in 1956.

questions.q: Polycythemia is disease related to ?
questions.e: Polycythemia is an abnormal increase in red blood cells, a blood disorder.

questions.q: Peru's government declared on environmental emergency in which area, where state oil firm petroperu last weekend spilled a crude oil shipment into surrounding water of the pacific ocean in 2024?
questions.e: The 2024 Petroperu spill at the Talara refinery affected Peru's northern coastal area.

questions.q: Which report of India was submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) on 30th December 2024?
questions.e: India submitted its fourth Biennial Update Report (BUR-4) to the UNFCCC on 30 December 2024.

questions.q: What is the primary cause of acid rain?
questions.e: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides form sulphuric and nitric acids that fall as acid rain.

questions.q: The 2023 Manipur crisis primarily involves violent classes between which two communities
questions.e: The 2023 Manipur violence was mainly between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities.

questions.q: In June 2025, the united states carried out airstrikes on Iranian nuclear sites under what operation name?
questions.e: The June 2025 US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites were called Operation Midnight Hammer.

questions.q: Who is the president of the European commission?
questions.e: Ursula von der Leyen is President of the European Commission.

questions.q: In 1994, Dishom guru Shibu Soren became president of
questions.e: Shibu Soren became chairman of the Jharkhand Area Autonomous Council (JAAC) formed in the mid-1990s.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important critical stage for irrigation in wheat crop?
questions.e: Crown Root Initiation (about 21 days after sowing) is the most critical irrigation stage for wheat.

questions.q: Ramgarh Hill tract was established in which year?
questions.e: The British formed the Ramgarh Hill Tract in 1780.

questions.q: Which British captain was sent to occupy palamu in the year 1771?
questions.e: Captain Jacob Camac was sent in 1771 to occupy Palamu.

questions.q: The habitat of Birhor tribe is called
questions.e: Birhor settlements are called Tanda.

questions.q: Tanginath Mandir is situated in which district of Jharkhand?
questions.e: Tanginath Dham, with its iron trident, is in Gumla district.

questions.q: Which one is the nutrient having special significance to carbohydrate rich crops and imparts disease resistance to crops, improves size and quality of flowers, fruits, vegetables and grains?
questions.e: Potassium aids carbohydrate formation, disease resistance and produce quality.

questions.q: The dormitory in munda tribal society is called
questions.e: The Munda youth dormitory is called Gitiora (Giti-ora).

questions.q: What is the name of the army chief that was sent by Mughal emperor Akbar in 1585 to attack the Nagvanshi ruler in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Akbar sent Shahbaz Khan Kambu in 1585 against the Nagvanshi ruler of Kokrah.

questions.q: Which Temple was made by Nagvanshi ruler Phani Mukut Rai in Sutiyambe?
questions.e: Nagvanshi king Phani Mukut Rai built a Surya (Sun) temple at Sutiyambe, per the official key.

questions.q: In Which scripture Jharkhand is called Pundric Desh.
questions.e: The Mahabharata refers to the region as Pundrik Desh.

questions.q: In which year Birsa Munda held the first meeting for Ulgulan at Dombari hill?
questions.e: Birsa Munda's Ulgulan meeting at Dombari Buru took place in December 1899.

questions.q: Wilt of Pigeon pea is a disease caused which of the following?
questions.e: Pigeon pea wilt is caused by the fungus Fusarium udum.

questions.q: Which of one is not a cereal crop?
questions.e: Pigeon pea (arhar) is a pulse, not a cereal.

questions.q: Which of the following is a potassic fertilizer?
questions.e: Muriate of Potash (MOP, KCl) is a potassic fertiliser.
